question: An analyst has forty pages of interview notes and has been asked to produce something the team can use in a workshop next week. What should she do first?
options: A) Ask Claude to produce the notes as a long document she can then trim down before the workshop.
B) Paste all forty pages into a conversation and ask Claude what the most important themes are.
C) Split the notes into separate files by interviewee so that each one can be discussed on its own.
D) Decide what the participants must be able to do with it, since that drives structure and format.
correct_answers: D) Decide what the participants must be able to do with it, since that drives structure and format.
explanations: Incorrect. Generating a deliverable before its purpose is settled usually means reworking it, and length is not the problem she is solving.
Incorrect. Extracting themes is useful later, but it does not answer what the workshop needs the material to do.
Incorrect. Organising by source is one possible structure, and choosing it now assumes an answer she has not worked out yet.
Correct. Format follows use. Knowing whether people will read, sort, discuss or annotate the material is what determines whether it should be a document, a table or a diagram.
